title: Doubao Mobile Assistant SAEP Public Comment Period Ends: Gradual Release of Screen Automation Permissions for Third-Party Applications

content_html:
On October 14, Douba Mobile Assistant announced that the 30-day public notice period for its Screen Automation Execution Protocol (SAEP) has ended, and it will gradually grant third-party applications access to screen automation operations. The protocol was launched together with the consumer version of Douba Mobile Assistant on September 14, and the Nubia NaviX Ultra equipped with this version was released on September 16.

According to the protocol design, during the public notice period, the assistant will only perform automated operations on system-built-in applications, ByteDance's applications, and third-party applications that have explicitly agreed to join the protocol; other applications will not be operated by default.

After the public notice period ends, the assistant will gradually grant operation permissions to applications that neither responded to the email nor joined the protocol, based on the risk level. Applications that have clearly refused will never be included in the operation scope. Developers can still declare refusal at any time, and the assistant will promptly disable the relevant operations. The current list of refused applications can be viewed and regularly updated through official channels.
